title: motion/v1
description: targets/<id>/motions/<n>.yaml (F24-R2; D-32 v3.34): a question put to the target's steward panel, opened by a steward of the target or a listed curator. It is decided when its window closes (policy.json vote_window_days after `date`), on the votes cast. An invitation opened by a curator passes when it is opened, and so does any motion opened by the only counted member of the panel; the invitee still joins only by their own steward record naming it. Append-only; versioned, never edited (D-34).

kind.description: `invite`: admit `subject.login` as a steward. `verify-writeup`: the panel verifies write-up `subject.writeup`. `authorship-threshold`: set the ledger threshold above which contributors are coauthors to `subject.threshold`.

note.description: For an invitation: the part of the work the invitee is asked for, in a sentence (an area of the proof). Free text, escaped where shown.

writeup.description: The write-up's number n in targets/<id>/writeup/<n>.yaml.

threshold.description: The ledger threshold (D-32): entries above it are coauthors.

opened_by.description: The login of the steward or curator who opened the motion.

settings.description: The voting settings in force when the motion was opened, copied from policy.json's panel (or its defaults) in the merge's parent tree; the gate refuses a copy that differs. The motion is decided by these, so a later change to policy.json never reaches a motion already open (D-32 v3.34).

date.description: The day the record was made (UTC). The gate refuses a record dated more than one day from its own clock, so a date cannot be written into an old window.

via.description: How the signature was made (D-3, D-32 v3.33): `ssh`, by the signer's own SSH key; `approval-key`, by the network's approval key through the service, for a login signed in with GitHub on the site, in which case `key` must equal the graph's keys/approval.pub in the merge's parent tree.

key.description: The SSH public key the signature verifies under: the steward's own (`via: ssh`) or the network's approval key (`via: approval-key`).

signature.description: An OpenSSH SSHSIG armored signature over the record's canonical body, made with the private half of `key`.
